scenes.contextualRelevance: Blumenthal's strong defense of Clinton against personal attacks suggests a deep understanding of the political climate and the challenges she has faced. The emphasis on shared values implies a deeper bond than just political expediency.

Blumenthal discusses the shared values and experiences that underpin their friendship, emphasizing their commitment to democracy and combating personal attacks in politics.
Blumenthal highlights Hillary Clinton's unique experience and qualifications for the presidency, mentioning her time in the White House and as Secretary of State.

text_to_speech: It is publicly known that you and Hillary Clinton are friends already for decades. Friendships in the political world are rare. What makes it that your friendship has survived? I have known Hillary for almost 30 years and I hope that when this conference takes place, she has been elected president. We share common values, political values, but also I think that these are deeply rooted in our own personal experiences. We have defended these values against all sorts of people who have used whatever means that they could. Many of them underhanded, in order to try and destroy reputations. To attack people personally. To engage in what we have called the politics of personal destruction, but for political advantage and gain. It is not only a bond of friendship, but rooted, I think, in our common devotion to advancing democracy in the country. It sounds like a cliché but there it is. We are a year apart in age, we grew up five miles from each other. We know very much who we are. So, I think that there is a rootedness as well in our commitment to engagement. Does she realize the enormity of the responsibility she will get when she is elected president? I think if anybody understands the responsibility of the presidency, it would be Hillary Clinton, having served in the White House with her husband and having been Secretary of State with another president: Barack Obama. There are very few people in American history who have had that sort of background who have risen to the presidency. She would be a rare person. Not only as the first woman but simply as a person to assume that office. Thank you, Sidney. I am much looking forward seeing you on the 12th of November in Amsterdam.
